newsitem.title: QATAR: QGPC signs oil condensate refinery memorandum - QN.
newsitem.headline: QGPC signs oil condensate refinery memorandum - QN.

text.p: Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC) and its foreign partners in the Qatargas and Rasgas liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects have signed a memorandum of understanding to set up an oil condensate refinery in the Gulf Arab state, the Qatar News Agency (QNA) reported on Tuesday.

The exported-orientated refinery at Ras Laffan is expected to be operational in 2001 at a capital cost of $340 million, QNA reported Qatar energy and industry minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah as saying.
Partners in Qatargas and Rasgas are Mobil Corp, Total SA, Marubeni Corp, Mitsui Corp, Nissho Iwai and Itochu.
The refinery at Ras Laffan would process condensate produced as a result of the exploitation of the massive offshore North Field which is the backbone of LNG development in Qatar.

Qatar currently produces 80,000 barrels per day (bpd) of condensate which is exported mainly to the Far East but output is expected to reach more than 200,000 bpd by the year 2000 when the North Field is tapped further by Qatargas and Rasgas.
A feasibility study would be carried out to determine the size of the proposed condensate refinery, QNA reported.
